# LSAT 2-Week Study Sprint for a 154 → 162 Goal

A focused 14-day plan for a Chicago student with **3 hours on weekdays** and **5 hours on weekends**. The plan prioritizes **Logical Reasoning**, includes **review blocks**, **rest time**, and ends with a **final-day strategy**.

## 14-Day LSAT Plan

| Day | Time Budget | Focus | Key Sessions | Goal |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3h | Baseline LR setup | 45m timed LR set; 60m review missed questions; 45m argument structure drill; 30m error log | Identify recurring LR mistakes |
| 2 | 3h | LR question types | 60m weaken/strengthen; 45m assumption family; 45m blind review; 30m break + notes | Build pattern recognition |
| 3 | 3h | Reading comp support | 45m passage mapping; 60m RC set; 45m review; 30m light LR recap | Improve speed and passage focus |
| 4 | 3h | LR flaw + inference | 60m flaw questions; 45m inference questions; 45m review; 30m rest/decompress | Reduce trap-answer errors |
| 5 | 3h | Mixed timed drill | 2 timed LR sections; 60m deep review; 30m error log cleanup | Strengthen pacing under pressure |
| 6 | 5h | Full practice test 1 | 3h 35m full PT under test conditions; 85m review of only flagged questions | Establish current test baseline |
| 7 | 5h | Practice test review | 2h review wrong answers; 1h blind review; 1h LR redo set; 1h rest/walk | Turn PT errors into patterns |
| 8 | 3h | LR core repair | 60m conditional logic; 45m parallel/parallel flaw; 45m review; 30m flash review | Sharpen logic chain accuracy |
| 9 | 3h | RC + LR balance | 45m RC timed set; 60m LR timed set; 45m review; 30m light drill | Maintain section balance |
| 10 | 3h | High-yield LR | 60m hardest LR type; 45m untimed accuracy set; 45m review; 30m rest | Improve accuracy before speed |
| 11 | 3h | Timing practice | 60m timed LR section; 60m review; 30m mini-drill; 30m break | Tighten pacing and decision-making |
| 12 | 5h | Full practice test 2 | 3h 35m full PT under test conditions; 85m review of only flagged questions | Measure progress toward 162 |
| 13 | 5h | Final review day | 2h PT review; 1h LR error log; 1h redo missed questions; 1h light walk/rest | Lock in lessons, avoid burnout |
| 14 | 3h | Final-day strategy | 45m light LR warm-up; 30m RC mapping; 30m confidence review; 45m logistics; 30m rest; 30m mental reset | Arrive fresh, calm, and ready |

## Weekly Focus and Execution

### Week 1: Build accuracy first
- Spend most of the week on **Logical Reasoning**, since that is the biggest score lever.
- Use a strict review method: for every missed question, note the **question type, wrong choice trap, and why the credited answer wins**.
- Keep one short daily break block so the work stays high quality.

### Week 2: Convert accuracy into test readiness
- Use the second half of the plan to **repeat weak LR types**, then confirm progress with another full practice test.
- Keep the final 48 hours lighter: more review, less grinding.
- Protect sleep and avoid adding new material at the end.

### Final-day strategy
- Do only **light warm-up questions**, not a full section.
- Pack everything early: ID, admissions ticket, snacks, water, charger, pencils, and layers for Chicago weather.
- Stop heavy studying the night before; aim for an early bedtime.
- On test day, use this pacing mindset:
  - First pass: answer cleanly and move on
  - Mark tough questions quickly
  - Return only if time remains
  - Trust your first well-supported answer
